subject: Biotechnology
title: Non-Invasive Prenatal Testing
description: A 60-second lesson on Non-Invasive Prenatal Testing.

hook.text: Fetal DNA floats in a pregnant mother's blood — a simple blood draw can detect Down syndrome without amniocentesis.

buildup.text: Cell-free fetal DNA makes up 10 to 20% of maternal plasma by the tenth week — sequencing counts chromosome fragments.

discovery.text: Excess chromosome 21 fragments indicate trisomy 21 — NIPT detects Down syndrome with over 99% sensitivity.

twist.text: False positives occur — confined placental mosaicism or maternal copy number variants mimic fetal abnormalities.

climax.text: NIPT now screens for microdeletions and single-gene disorders — expanding beyond trisomies to hundreds of conditions.

punchline.text: A blood test replaces a needle — NIPT makes prenatal screening safe and simple.

quiz.question: What causes false positives in NIPT?
options: The mother's DNA interferes with all fetal DNA detection
Confined placental mosaicism or maternal copy number variants can mimic fetal abnormalities
The test cannot distinguish between chromosomes 21 and 18

details.summary: Non-invasive prenatal testing analyzes fetal DNA circulating in maternal blood to screen for chromosomal abnormalities including Down syndrome, trisomy 18, and trisomy 13 without risk of miscarriage. It has dramatically reduced the need for invasive amniocentesis and chorionic villus sampling.
details.whyItMatters: NIPT transformed prenatal screening by providing highly accurate results from a simple maternal blood draw as early as 10 weeks. It avoids the approximately 0.
takeaways: Fetal DNA in maternal blood enables chromosomal screening without invasion
NIPT detects over 99 percent of Down syndrome cases from a blood draw
It has reduced invasive amniocentesis procedures by over 50 percent globally

faq.question: How is fetal DNA present in the mother's blood?
faq.answer: Placental cells shed DNA fragments into maternal circulation beginning around 5 weeks of pregnancy. By 10 weeks, fetal DNA comprises about 10 percent of total cell-free DNA in maternal blood. This fraction increases throughout pregnancy. The DNA is cleared within hours after delivery.

faq.question: Is NIPT a diagnostic or screening test?
faq.answer: NIPT is a screening test with high sensitivity and specificity but not 100 percent accuracy. Positive results require confirmatory diagnostic testing through amniocentesis or CVS. False positive rates are low but exist, especially for rare trisomies.
